title: A K256 shared operand on B300 needs four K64 TMA boxes before four warp-local MMA partials can be emitted
backend: native_cuda warp MMA proposal; CuTe-DSL and native tcgen05 single-box routes remain separate
executor_revision: sm_103a@b00b2b8fda331011cad519d2817804ee7951fab3; external broker-bound diagnostic scripts, not a formal Executor receipt

evidence.note: The K64-box TMA and four-warp mma.sync prototype produced bitwise-equal complete outputs on both short-K shapes across five input distributions, with every input preserved. The prototype is outside the Compiler.

Under one broker-exclusive CUPTI comparison, the TMA prototype, selected-load Triton and official CAKE medians were 3.392, 5.856 and 3.040 microseconds. All five round outputs matched bitwise, each arm launched one kernel, and each arm's maximum within-round CV was below 5%. This is a custom diagnostic, not formal Evaluation admission.
The alternate single K256 TMA descriptor was refused by cuTensorMapEncodeTiled with CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE before kernel launch. Its report cannot be used as a performance result.

The previous equality check rejected a K64 descriptor for a K256 shared staging buffer. The proposed structural rule admits only boxes that exactly match the buffer or evenly tile its final shared-memory axis. The existing CuTe and native tcgen05 emitters explicitly refuse the tiled route.

A swapped A/B TMA prototype retained exact bits across both short-K shapes and five input distributions while keeping the output register axes in public row-major order. Its B16 native/selected-Triton/official medians were 3.393/5.888/3.040 microseconds, with all three maximum within-round CVs below 5%. B1 official CV exceeded 5%, so its latency is descriptive.

The existing k_ranges canonicalizer merges adjacent ranges and erases four equal K partitions. A separate k_partitions field preserves ordered warp-local FP32 partials and their left-associated sum; common verification accepts the complete staged Schedule while current emitters refuse it by name.

The first Compiler-emitted native kernel passed CPU compilation but swapped A/B TMA descriptor parameters. Ready-barrier expected bytes never completed; the task-owned broker job was cancelled, then GPU contexts and queues were verified clear. Successor 212b6f7a corrected the descriptor order and added a source-boundary regression check.

Normal Python native_source authoring under Compiler commit 4da760be produced clean AOT artifacts and completed all ten short-K shape/distribution cases. Every native output matched the frozen official CAKE output bitwise, all prepared inputs remained unchanged, and the task lease was released before host validation.

Five alternating-order cold-L2 CUPTI rounds measured Compiler native 3.424, selected-load Triton 5.888 and official CAKE 3.008 microseconds for B16/N1024/K1024. Each arm had one CUDA kernel, all round outputs and inputs passed, and maximum within-round CVs were 4.888%, 2.502% and 4.382%, respectively. This broker-bound custom diagnostic is not a formal Evaluation receipt.

For B1/N128/K720 the corresponding medians were native 2.815, selected-load Triton 4.639 and official CAKE 2.656 microseconds, with complete bitwise outputs and one kernel per arm. The official arm maximum within-round CV was 7.510%, so the external latency edge remains descriptive.

Under one broker-exclusive five-round cold-L2 CUPTI assay, old Triton to final native CUDA median paired speedup was 36.045x; final to official CAKE median paired latency ratio was 1.061x. All five rounds had bitwise-equal complete outputs, unchanged inputs, and exactly one kernel per arm. The old/final edge passed the 5% within-round CV gate. The final/official edge failed that gate because the official arm CV reached 8.137%. This custom diagnostic is not a formal Evaluation receipt.

Under one broker-exclusive five-round cold-L2 CUPTI assay, old Triton to final native CUDA median paired speedup was 30.972x; final to official CAKE median paired latency ratio was 1.138x. All five rounds had bitwise-equal complete outputs, unchanged inputs, and exactly one kernel per arm. The old/final edge passed the 5% within-round CV gate. The final/official edge passed that gate. This custom diagnostic is not a formal Evaluation receipt.

Under one broker-exclusive five-round cold-L2 CUPTI assay, old Triton to final selected-load Triton, two groups and two stages median paired speedup was 11.722x; final to official CAKE median paired latency ratio was 1.151x. All five rounds had bitwise-equal complete outputs, unchanged inputs, and exactly one kernel per arm. The old/final edge passed the 5% within-round CV gate. The final/official edge passed that gate. This custom diagnostic is not a formal Evaluation receipt.

A bounded K3072 depth-one hypothesis kept the same Workload, four FP32 partials, two execution groups, oracle and cold-L2 CUPTI protocol. It passed five input distributions bitwise, with unchanged inputs and one kernel per arm. Five paired rounds measured s1 37.760 versus retained s2 24.545 microseconds; median paired s1/s2 latency was 1.538x, and all three arms had maximum within-round CV below 1.6%. No promotion: the existing two-stage authored route remains the qualified diagnostic representative.

observation: The B300 gap is partly an emission-mechanism gap. Direct selected-K loads reduced the largest historical TinyGEMM slowdown, but the two short-K fixtures remain slower than official CAKE. A scalar global-to-shared warp-MMA prototype was numerically exact yet much slower. Replacing its copies with four K64 TMA boxes made the B16 prototype nearly match the official kernel. A K256 box is rejected by the device API, so describing K256 staging with one K256 descriptor is not a valid shortcut. The existing common verifier's exact box/staging equality prevented the K64-box plan even before backend admission. Swapping the MMA operand orientation preserves bitwise outputs on both short-K fixtures and makes the accumulator axes match the public row-major output, avoiding a new output-layout abstraction. The existing k_ranges field merges adjacent intervals, so it cannot name the four distinct warp partials; that requires a separate typed K-partition commitment. The normal Python-authored Compiler successor 4da760be now emits the TMA warp-MMA route and passes all ten short-K bitwise peer cases. The B16 paired custom CUPTI diagnostic is stable and narrows the original gap to about 14%; B1 retains an external-CV failure. This is implementation evidence, while formal Evaluation remains blocked by B300-M4 broker admission identity rather than by kernel correctness. A final same-run three-arm comparison under authored Compiler commit 4da760be measured paired old-to-final gains of 36.045x, 30.972x and 11.722x for the three fixed TinyGEMM shapes. All old/final edges passed the 5% within-round CV gate; the B16/B64 external edges passed, while B1 official CAKE CV failed. The Compiler-native route applies to the two short-K fixtures and the selected-load Triton route to the K3072 fixture. A successor depth-one ablation on B64 was numerically exact but 1.538x slower than the retained two-stage route in a stable same-run comparison. No stage-depth widening or promotion follows.
proposed_change: Admit a declared TMA descriptor box that evenly tiles the final axis of one shared staging buffer, while each existing emitter refuses a route it cannot emit. Then add a bounded native_cuda mma.sync path whose Schedule declares the four compute groups, four producer groups per operand, K256 stage and K64 descriptor boxes, named readiness/synchronization, four FP32 partials, CTA reduction and BF16 bias epilogue. Preserve exact target and bitwise Workload gates; do not route by operator name or copy the external kernel into the backend. A formal B300-M4 comparison also needs an Executor successor that accepts the existing broker's own admission receipt without inventing GPUQ_JOB_ID. Add ordered k_partitions to the MMA data model with complete nonoverlapping coverage, one execution group per partition, and instruction-aligned boundaries; keep every current emitter refusing it until the native warp-MMA route exists. The provisional core and NVIDIA task commits implement the typed route, but integration through maintained branches and a formal Executor successor that consumes broker-issued admission are still required before closing this Finding or publishing platform result rows. Do not upgrade these custom broker diagnostics into published result rows: the formal sm_103a Executor admission still expects GPUQ_JOB_ID that the B300-M4 broker does not inject; keep the Finding open until a successor preserves the measurement contract and completes formal replay.
